introduction: The Eagle Nebula is shown through infrared observations from Spitzer and visible-light observations from Hubble.
observe: Compare the apparent density of the pillars in visible and infrared light.
Look for stars or structures that become easier to distinguish in one view.
explanation: Different wavelength ranges interact differently with the dust in the nebula, so the same region does not reveal the same structure in every view.
colorMethod: The composite places infrared and visible-light views together for comparison; the panels do not represent one uniform visible-color exposure.
whyItMatters: Changing wavelength can reveal information hidden in a familiar visible-light image.
